title: Add an expires_at field and TTL index to the Secrets model
description: In applications/db-models/repos/onfinance-db-model-master/onfinance_db_model_master/models.py, class Secrets(Document) (lines 8-15): add expires_at = DateTimeField(required=True) and meta = {"collection": "secrets", "indexes": [{"fields": ["expires_at"], "expireAfterSeconds": 0}]}. Pin the collection name explicitly so the existing collection is kept. Every writer must set expires_at from the task 1 schedule. Backfill existing secrets documents with an expires_at per the schedule in qa first, then prod, after a mongodump backup. Deploy dev -> qa -> prod per sdlc/policy.json releaseProcess (1 approval, rollback plan required) and honour any changeFreeze in applications/db-models/env/*.json.
acceptanceCriteria: python -c "from onfinance_db_model_master.models import Secrets; print(Secrets._meta['indexes'])" prints an index on expires_at with expireAfterSeconds 0, and Secrets._meta['collection'] == 'secrets'
Saving a Secrets document without expires_at raises mongoengine ValidationError
In qa, db.secrets.getIndexes() lists expires_at_1 with expireAfterSeconds 0, and db.secrets.countDocuments({expires_at: {$exists: false}}) returns 0 after the backfill

verificationMethod.description: Re-run probe-schemas on db-models/onfinance-db-model-master. Expected: the SARIF export for models.py shows the Secrets class with a retention field and TTL index. SCH-RET-02 fully clears only once task 3 also lands, because the rule covers both classes at the same path.

rootCause.description: The Secrets model was written as a plain credential store with no expiry field or TTL index, so Zerodha passwords, 2FA seeds, API secrets and access tokens are never removed after their purpose ends.
